artworks.title: Medea about to Kill her Children
artworks.description: Delacroix's Romantic Medea crouches in a cave with her two sons, dagger ready, the Colchian sorceress frozen at the edge of Euripides' revenge. The Louvre canvas made her fury the nineteenth century's defining image of the abandoned wife who will burn Corinth to ash — motherhood and murder in a single charged pose.

artworks.title: Medea
artworks.description: Sandys' Pre-Raphaelite half-length shows Medea as enchantress at her work: mixing the poison for Creusa's bridal gift, a coral necklace and magic vessels before her. The painting isolates the Colchian witch's craft rather than the slaughter — intelligence and dread in equal measure. Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery.

artworks.title: Jason and Medea
artworks.description: Waterhouse stages the Colchian alliance before the blood: Medea brews the charm that will protect Jason from Aeëtes' fire-breathing bulls, while the hero waits at her side. The painting catches the romance that Euripides will later destroy — the sorceress still helping the Greek who will abandon her. Private collection; widely reproduced from the artist's late myth cycle.

artworks.title: Vision of Medea
artworks.description: Turner's swirling vision places Medea amid the supernatural machinery of her revenge — spells, dragons and the haze of Corinthian catastrophe. Painted in Rome and now associated with the Tate/National Gallery circle of Turner's myth subjects, it dissolves Euripides' sorceress into light and storm rather than a single dagger-blow.

artworks.title: Medea
artworks.description: Gentileschi's Baroque Medea is a solitary half-length of the Colchian witch at work — focused, armed with her craft, already past pity. One of the rare early modern images to give Medea the same fierce agency Artemisia gave Judith, it anchors the figure in the painter's gallery of wronged women who act.

films.title: Medea
films.description: Maria Callas' only film role: Pasolini's Medea as priestess, exile and avenger — the Colchian sorceress who burns her Greek marriage to ash.

films.title: Medea
films.description: Von Trier's stark television Medea, after Dreyer's unrealised script: the revenge in mud and mist, without opera's velvet.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Harryhausen's Medea is the Colchian ally who helps Jason win the fleece — the romance before Euripides' later blood.

music.title: Médée
music.description: Cherubini's French Médée is the great Classical Medea opera: the abandoned wife whose fury Callas later made legendary in Italian revival.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant brings Medea into the crossroads as a witch of the mountain — Colchian craft offered to Melinoë on the road against Chronos.
